brackets.note: One schedule covers single, joint and head of household filers. Senate Bill 392 (2026) cut every rate for taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2026. The statute prints $1,950.50 plus 4.58% of the excess over $60,000 for the top bracket, which these brackets reproduce. Tax Foundation still shows the 2025 rates (2.22%, 2.96%, 3.33%, 4.44%, 4.82%), which predate the bill. PolicyEngine matches the statute.

personalExemption.note: $2,000 for each exemption (filer, spouse and each dependent). Set in statute and not indexed. Tax Foundation agrees.

rules.note: Local flag set to true for city service fees: Charleston's overview says employers withhold $3.00 a week from employees. Other cities were not checked. Contribution flags checked on 2026-11-12 against PolicyEngine US 2.118.6 (oracle/flags.py), which moves this state's tax by the same amount as this engine for 401k, HSA, IRA and health premium contributions. FSA and commuter benefits are not PolicyEngine inputs and rest on the state starting from federal income. Not read in the state's own instructions. No employee payroll contribution: the US Department of Labor's comparison lists worker unemployment contributions only in Alaska, New Jersey and Pennsylvania and disability insurance only in California, Hawaii, New Jersey, New York and Rhode Island, and no paid leave or similar program with an employee contribution was found for this state on 2026-11-12.
notes: West Virginia has no standard deduction. Taxable income is federal AGI, with state modifications, less exemptions.
Some West Virginia cities charge people who work there a flat weekly service fee. Charleston's is $3 a week. Not included.
Not modeled: filers with federal AGI of $10,000 or less can exclude up to $10,000 of earned income.
Not modeled: the low-income family tax credit.
From tax year 2027 rates can fall further under the revenue trigger in West Virginia Code 11-21-4h, so check the rates each year.
